description: Ten short European city breaks turn Bordeaux, Reykjavik, Berlin, Vienna, Bologna, Lisbon, Copenhagen, Cadiz, Thessaloniki and Palermo into compact food histories built from markets, restaurants, local rituals and the surrounding landscape.

s08e01.description: A weekend in Bordeaux moves from ceps and market produce to a wine competition and the nearby Atlantic coast, where oysters and mussels lead Rick back to steak frites with Bordelaise sauce.

s08e02.description: In and around Reykjavik, Rick explores Icelandic cod, lamb from the fjords and a food culture learning to treat stark local ingredients as strengths rather than limitations.

s08e03.description: Berlin's history and restless contemporary food scene share the itinerary as Rick samples modern vegetable-led cooking, including sunflower-seed purée and artichoke flans, alongside the city's older habits.

s08e04.description: Vienna supplies tafelspitz, goulash and schnitzel, but Rick also follows city vineyards, coffeehouses, strudel and Sachertorte to understand the rituals surrounding its imperial comfort food.

s08e05.description: Fresh egg pasta dominates Bologna as Rick watches tortellini, tagliatelle, ravioli and lasagne being made, then wanders the market and the university quarter beneath the city's medieval towers.

s08e06.description: Lisbon's seafood, salt cod and custard tarts lead into the Portuguese empire's culinary legacy, while pork with clams and the St Anthony sardine festival reveal a city happiest when eating in public.

s08e07.description: New Nordic ideas of foraging, pickling and seasonality sit beside smørrebrød, pastries and pork belly, letting Rick compare Copenhagen's fashionable restaurants with the everyday food beneath them.

s08e08.description: Cadiz blends Phoenician and Arab history with tapas, tuna and manzanilla; Rick adds arroz verde and flamenco eggs while exploring a port whose food has absorbed centuries of arrivals.

s08e09.description: Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman layers remain visible in Thessaloniki's seafood and meze, as Rick cooks with peaches and mussels and finds hearty veal and aubergine stews behind the city's café culture.

s08e10.description: Palermo's Arab, North African, French, Spanish and Italian inheritances collide in markets and street food, culminating in the feast of Santa Rosalia, a duchess's cooking lesson and Rick's marsala chicken.
